mainTopic: The power of תשובה, how to confess (וידוי), and when sins should be revealed or covered
overview: The גמרא opens with a series of 'גדולה תשובה' sayings. Each one shows a different power of תשובה: it overrides a לא תעשה, brings the גאולה closer, turns sins into שגגות or even זכיות (depending on whether it comes מאהבה or מיראה), lengthens life, and, through one person's תשובה, brings forgiveness to the whole world. רבה בר מרי contrasts people, who may not forgive even after words, with ה׳, who accepts words of תשובה and values them like a voluntary קרבן. רב יהודה defines a complete בעל תשובה as one who faces the same temptation again and holds back. The גמרא then discusses when a sin should be made public and when it should stay covered. It also teaches that a repeated sin is easily forgiven only three times. Next comes a debate over whether to re-confess on a later יום הכיפורים sins already forgiven, and whether one must spell out the sin, with משה and דוד as examples of the two approaches. The עמוד ends with warnings about the comfort of רשעים and the dangers of authority, illustrated by what רב said on his way to judge. רבא's parallel saying begins at the end and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Repentance overrides a Torah prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that תשובה is so great that it overrides a לא תעשה in the Torah. He proves it from a פסוק in ירמיהו that compares Israel to a wife who left her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Repentance is great, because it pushes aside a Torah prohibition. As the verse says: 'If a man sends away his wife, and she leaves him and marries another man, can he go back to her? Wouldn't that land be badly defiled? Yet you have been unfaithful with many lovers, and still return to Me, says ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן opens a list of sayings about the greatness of תשובה. He says תשובה is strong enough to override a Torah prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids a man to remarry his divorced wife after she married someone else. ירמיהו compares Israel to such a wife who was unfaithful to ה׳, which by that law should block her return. Even so, ה׳ says 'return to Me', so תשובה overrides what the prohibition would normally block.

keyTerms.meaning: Great is repentance (the opening formula of each saying)
A negative commandment, a Torah prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק does not mention the prohibition itself. It is in דברים כ״ד:ד (a divorced wife who remarried may not return to her first husband). ירמיהו is hinting at that law and showing that תשובה works even where that kind of law would forbid a return.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: Great is repentance
for it overrides a prohibition that is in the Torah

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לֵאמֹר הֵן יְשַׁלַּח אִישׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ
phrases.english: as it is stated: 'Saying: If a man sends away his wife'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו ג:א

phrases.english: and she goes from him and becomes another man's wife
may he return to her again?
Would that land not be greatly defiled?
And you have been unfaithful with many lovers
yet return to Me, says ה׳.'
phrases.notes: Despite the prohibition, ה׳ invites Israel back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the series of 'גדולה תשובה' statements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשובה overrides a לא תעשה: Israel may return to ה׳ even where the parallel marital law would forbid a return.

steps.title: Repentance brings the redemption closer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן says תשובה brings the גאולה closer, based on ישעיהו. The גמרא explains the פסוק: the redeemer comes because people in יעקב repent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן said: Repentance is great, because it brings the redemption closer. As the verse says: 'A redeemer will come to Zion, and to those in Jacob who turn back from sin.' Why will the redeemer come to Zion? Because there are people in Jacob who turn back from sin.
steps.whatsHappening: A second 'גדולה תשובה' saying: תשובה speeds up the גאולה. The גמרא then reads the פסוק to show it is a cause-and-effect statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק could just list two things: a redeemer comes, and penitents exist. The גמרא's question 'מה טעם' reads the second half as the reason for the first. The redeemer comes because Israel does תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who turn back from sin

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan said: Great is repentance
for it brings the redemption closer
as it is stated: 'And a redeemer will come to Zion'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו נ״ט:כ

phrases.english: 'and to those in Jacob who turn back from sin'
What is the reason that 'a redeemer will come to Zion'?
Because 'there are those in Jacob who turn back from sin.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent praise of תשובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשובה hastens the גאולה, since the redeemer's coming is caused by Israel's repentance.

steps.title: Repentance turns intentional sins into accidental ones
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that after תשובה, a person's זדונות count as שגגות. He proves it from הושע, where an עון (intentional sin) is called stumbling.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Repentance is great, because a person's intentional sins become like accidental sins. As the verse says: 'Return, Israel, to ה׳ your God, for you have stumbled in your sin.' Now an 'עון' is an intentional sin, and yet the verse calls it a stumble.
steps.whatsHappening: A third 'גדולה תשובה' saying: once a person does תשובה, his deliberate sins are treated like mistakes. The גמרא spells out how the פסוק shows this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עון means a deliberate sin. Stumbling (כשלת) describes an accident. Since the פסוק about returning to ה׳ uses stumbling language for an עון, ריש לקיש learns that תשובה reduces intentional sins to the level of accidental ones.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: Great is repentance
for his intentional sins become like unintentional ones
as it is stated: 'Return, Israel, to ה׳ your God'
phrases.notes: הושע י״ד:ב

phrases.english: 'for you have stumbled in your iniquity'
Now 'iniquity' is an intentional sin
and yet the verse calls it a stumble.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ כִּשְׁגָגוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third praise of תשובה. This one becomes the subject of the next challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through תשובה, זדונות are counted as שגגות.

steps.title: ריש לקיש elsewhere says sins become merits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש with his own other statement: תשובה turns זדונות into זכיות, not just into שגגות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But ריש לקיש said: Repentance is great, because a person's intentional sins become like merits. As the verse says: 'When a wicked man turns from his wickedness and does justice and righteousness, he will live because of them!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sees a contradiction between two statements of ריש לקיש. One says sins become accidental sins, and the other says they become merits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שגגה is still a sin, only a lighter one, while a זכות is something good. The two statements give two different results for the same act of תשובה. The proof for 'merits' comes from the word עליהם, 'because of them': he lives through all his deeds, even the sins.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Reish Lakish say: Great is repentance
for his intentional sins become like merits
as it is stated: 'And when a wicked man turns from his wickedness'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל ל״ג:י״ט

phrases.english: 'and does justice and righteousness'
'he shall live through them!'
phrases.notes: 'Them' includes even his earlier sins, which now earn him life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 3 using another statement by the same אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's statement that זדונות become שגגות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same אמורא elsewhere says זדונות become זכיות. That is a much stronger result, so the two statements contradict each other.

steps.title: Repentance from love versus repentance from fear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both statements are true for different kinds of תשובה. תשובה מאהבה turns sins into merits, and תשובה מיראה turns them into accidental sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, the person repented out of love. There, the person repented out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by assigning each statement to a different type of תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who returns out of love for ה׳ gets the bigger result: his sins become merits. Someone who returns out of fear of punishment gets a smaller result: his sins are only reduced to שגגות. So the strength of תשובה depends on the motive behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
Here... there (each statement refers to a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: תשובה מאהבה makes זדונות into זכיות. תשובה מיראה makes זדונות into שגגות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic idea in the laws of תשובה: the motive behind returning decides how fully the past sins are changed.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, when he repents out of love
there, when he repents out of fear.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן מֵאַהֲבָה, כָּאן מִיִּרְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements describe the same תשובה, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: תשובה מאהבה turns sins into merits, and תשובה מיראה turns them into accidental sins.

steps.title: Repentance lengthens a person's life
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני, quoting רבי יונתן, says תשובה adds years to a person's life, based on a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Repentance is great, because it lengthens a person's years. As the verse says: 'When a wicked man turns from his wickedness, he will live.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the list of 'גדולה תשובה' sayings and adds another one: תשובה lengthens life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק promises that a רשע who returns 'will live'. רבי יונתן reads this literally: a person who might have died early because of his sins is given more years once he does תשובה.
steps.whatToRemember: The list so far: תשובה overrides a לא תעשה, brings the גאולה closer, transforms sins (into שגגות or זכיות depending on the motive), and lengthens life.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:

phrases.aramaic: גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמַּאֲרֶכֶת שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: Great is repentance, for it lengthens a person's years
as it is stated: 'When a wicked man turns from his wickedness'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל י״ח:כ״ז

phrases.english: 'he shall live.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the ריש לקיש contradiction, the גמרא resumes the list of praises of תשובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשובה lengthens a person's life.

steps.title: People may not forgive an insult, and words may not be enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reports a teaching from ארץ ישראל in the name of רבה בר מרי. When one person insults another, it is unclear whether the victim will forgive at all. Even if he does, it is unclear whether words alone will be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: In ארץ ישראל they say in the name of רבה בר מרי: Come and see that the way of people is not like the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא. If a person insults his friend with words, maybe the friend will forgive him and maybe he won't. And even if he will forgive, maybe words will be enough and maybe they won't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new teaching about תשובה. It starts by describing how people forgive, so it can contrast that with how ה׳ forgives in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first half of a comparison. It lists two doubts about human forgiveness: whether it will come at all, and whether words alone can earn it. The next step will show that neither doubt exists with ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל (west of בבל)
The way of flesh and blood, meaning human behavior

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי:
phrases.english: They say in the West (Eretz Yisrael) in the name of Rabba bar Mari:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Come and see that unlike the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood:
The way of flesh and blood:
if one insults his friend with words,
it is uncertain whether the friend will be appeased by him
or will not be appeased by him.
And if you say he will be appeased by him,
it is uncertain whether he will be appeased by words alone
or will not be appeased by words alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching that continues the praise of תשובה from steps 1-6, the series that began with רבי יוחנן. Instead of a 'גדולה תשובה' formula, it opens a comparison between human forgiveness and ה׳'s forgiveness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Human forgiveness is uncertain, and even when it comes, words alone may not earn it.

steps.title: ה׳ forgives a private sin with words alone
steps.stepSummary: Unlike people, הקדוש ברוך הוא accepts words of תשובה for a sin done in private. The source is הושע: take words with you and return to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with הקדוש ברוך הוא, if a person does a sin in private, ה׳ is appeased by words, as the פסוק says: 'Take words with you and return to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the second half of the comparison. With ה׳ there is no doubt: words of תשובה are accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both human doubts are removed at once. Forgiveness is certain, and words alone are enough. The teaching is limited to a sin בסתר (in private), probably because a public sin also involves the חילול השם it caused.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean words alone fix a sin against another person. The case here is a sin against ה׳ done in private. The previous step already showed that people may need more than words.

phrases.english: But the Holy One, Blessed be He:
if a person commits a sin in private,
He is appeased by him with words,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״קְחוּ עִמָּכֶם דְּבָרִים וְשׁוּבוּ אֶל ה׳״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'Take with you words and return to God.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast that step 7 began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ accepts words of תשובה for a private sin.

steps.title: ה׳ treats תשובה as a favor and as if bulls were offered
steps.stepSummary: Two more levels are added. ה׳ treats the תשובה as a good deed done for Him (from 'וקח טוב'). The פסוק also counts it as if the person offered bulls (from 'ונשלמה פרים שפתינו').
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but He considers it a favor done for Him, as it says: 'And accept that which is good.' And not only that, but the פסוק counts it for him as if he offered bulls, as it says: 'We will pay for bulls with our lips.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds up the praise of תשובה step by step using 'ולא עוד' ('and not only that'). Each level comes from the same פסוק in הושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First level: ה׳ accepts the words (step 8). Second level: ה׳ is actually grateful, as if the person did Him a kindness. Third level: the words of תשובה are valued like real קרבנות of bulls.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but even more
Considers it a favor, feels grateful to him
The פסוק counts it for him
We will pay for bulls with our lips

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁמַּחְזִיק לוֹ טוֹבָה,
phrases.english: And not only that, but He considers it a favor done for Him,
as it says: 'And accept that which is good.'

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁמַּעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב
phrases.english: And not only that, but the verse credits him
as if he had offered bulls,
as it says: 'So we will render for bulls the offering of our lips.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁמַּחְזִיק לוֹ טוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds further levels on top of the basic acceptance taught in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשובה is treated as a favor to ה׳ and counted as if the person offered bulls.

steps.title: The bulls count as a voluntary offering, not a required one
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think the 'bulls' are only like required קרבנות (חובה). A פסוק proves they count as voluntary gifts (נדבה): 'I will love them freely.'
steps.simpleTranslation: In case you would say these are only like required bulls, the פסוק teaches: 'I will heal their turning away, I will love them as a free gift (נדבה).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible misunderstanding of the previous step. It brings a פסוק to prove that תשובה is valued like a voluntary קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן חובה only fulfills an obligation. A קרבן נדבה is given out of love and is more precious. The word 'נדבה' in the פסוק shows that תשובה earns the higher level.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest you say; in case you might think

steps.whatToRemember: רבה בר מרי's teaching builds up in levels: ה׳ accepts words → treats it as a favor → counts it as bulls → and as voluntary bulls (נדבה).

phrases.english: Lest you say these are obligatory bulls,
the verse teaches:
'I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely (as a free-will gift).'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר פָּרֵי חוֹבָה, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the 'bulls' from step 9 and proves they are voluntary offerings.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'bulls' of תשובה count as נדבה, not חובה.

steps.title: One person's תשובה brings forgiveness to the whole world
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר: תשובה is so great that when one person repents, the whole world is forgiven. The proof is that the פסוק says 'My anger turned away from him' (singular), not 'from them'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר used to say: תשובה is great, because for the sake of one person who repented, the whole world is forgiven. As the פסוק says: 'I will heal their turning away, I will love them freely, for My anger has turned away from him.' It does not say 'from them,' but 'from him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another praise of תשובה from a ברייתא. It uses the same פסוק in הושע that ended the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the פסוק is plural ('their turning away,' 'I will love them'), but the reason given is singular ('from him'). רבי מאיר reads this to mean that because one person repented, everyone was healed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
For My anger has turned away from him

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir would say:
Great is repentance,
for on account of one individual who repented,
the entire world is forgiven,
as it says: 'I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely,
for My anger has turned away from him.'
It does not say 'from them,' but 'from him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new praise of תשובה that builds on the same פסוק quoted at the end of step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תשובה of one individual brings forgiveness to the entire world.

steps.title: What counts as a true בעל תשובה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we can tell that someone has fully done תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of a true בעל תשובה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. This sets up רב יהודה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After all this praise of תשובה, the גמרא wants a practical test. It asks what shows that a person's תשובה is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of a (complete) penitent?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from praising תשובה to defining when it is complete.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A clear test that shows someone's תשובה is complete.

steps.title: Facing the same temptation and holding back
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers: the same sin comes to him a first and second time, and he is saved from it. He then shows exactly what he means: the same woman, at the same time, in the same place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: For example, the chance to do the sin came to him a first time and a second time, and he held back from it. רב יהודה showed what he meant: with the same woman, at the same time, in the same place.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question from step 12 and gives a clear test for complete תשובה. He then spells out the exact conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Avoiding a sin when the situation has changed proves little. True תשובה shows when every condition is the same as when he sinned before, and this time he says no. The added details make the test exact.

keyTerms.meaning: Was saved from it, held back

steps.whatToRemember: A complete בעל תשובה is someone who meets the exact same temptation (same person, time, and place) and holds back.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a person's תשובה is worthless until he is tested. It describes the clearest proof that the תשובה is complete.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
For example, where the opportunity to sin came to his hand
a first time and a second time
and he was saved from it.
Rav Yehuda demonstrated:
with the same woman,
at the same time, in the same place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: כְּגוֹן שֶׁבָּאת לְיָדוֹ דְּבַר עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A complete בעל תשובה faces the same sin opportunity again, under identical conditions, and holds back.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the famous definition of תשובה גמורה later brought by the רמב״ם in הלכות תשובה.

steps.title: Two verses clash: should a sin be covered or not?
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted by רב יהודה, points out that one פסוק praises a person whose sin is covered, while another says a person who covers his sins will not succeed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: רב pointed out a contradiction. One verse says, 'Fortunate is the one whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.' Another verse says, 'One who covers his transgressions will not succeed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows two פסוקים that seem to say opposite things about hiding your sins. This sets up the answers in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in תהלים calls a person 'fortunate' when his sin is covered, so it sounds good to keep sins private. The verse in משלי says one who covers his sins 'will not succeed,' so it sounds like you must confess openly. Both cannot apply to the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: Points out a contradiction (literally 'throws' two sources against each other)
It is written... and it is written (the standard way to set two verses against each other)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: Rav raised a contradiction —
phrases.notes: Attribution merged into this step.

phrases.english: It is written: 'Fortunate is he whose transgression is forgiven,
phrases.notes: תהלים לב:א

phrases.english: whose sin is covered,'
phrases.notes: This sounds like keeping the sin hidden is good.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'He who covers his transgressions will not succeed'!
phrases.notes: משלי כח:יג. This sounds like hiding sins is bad.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about תשובה: whether a sinner should confess publicly.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the two פסוקים about covering sins fit together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק praises covering a sin and the other condemns it, which looks like a direct contradiction.

steps.title: Answer one: it depends whether the sin is already public
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction is solved: one verse speaks about a sin everyone already knows about, and the other speaks about a sin nobody knows about.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. This verse is about a sin that is publicly known. That verse is about a sin that is not publicly known.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers his own contradiction by saying each verse is about a different kind of sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sin is already public, hiding it is wrong ('will not succeed'), so the person should show his תשובה openly too. If the sin is private, it is better to keep it covered ('fortunate is the one whose sin is covered') and not spread it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
This one... that one (splitting two sources into two cases)
A sin that is publicly known

phrases.english: It is not difficult: this one is about a publicized sin,
phrases.notes: Here one should not cover it, so 'he who covers will not succeed' applies.

phrases.english: that one is about a sin that is not publicized.
phrases.notes: Here covering it is good, so 'fortunate is he whose sin is covered' applies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (each verse applies to a different situation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both verses seem to speak about every sin, so they clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: A sin already known should not be hidden; a private sin should stay covered.

steps.title: Answer two: sins against people versus sins against ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives a different answer: one verse is about sins between people, and the other is about sins between a person and ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב נחמן: Here it is about sins between a person and his fellow. There it is about sins between a person and ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא offers another way to solve the same contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a sin against another person, the sinner should not hide it ('will not succeed'). Making it known helps others convince the hurt person to forgive him. For a sin only against ה׳, he can keep it covered, since only ה׳ needs to forgive him.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there (another way of splitting two sources)
Between a person and his fellow (sins against people)
Between a person and ה׳ (sins against ה׳)

phrases.aramaic: רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Zutra bar Toviya said in the name of Rav Nachman:
phrases.notes: Attribution for the second answer.

phrases.english: Here it is about sins between a person and his fellow,
phrases.notes: Do not cover them: 'he who covers will not succeed.'

phrases.english: there it is about sins between a person and God.
phrases.notes: These may stay covered: 'fortunate is he whose sin is covered.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different way to split the cases than step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by type of sin rather than by whether it is known
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verses seem to clash about all sins.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sins against people should be confessed openly; sins against ה׳ may be kept private.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers explain when to confess openly: (1) if the sin is already public, or (2) if the sin was against another person.

steps.title: Forgiven three times, but not a fourth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי בר יהודה: a person who does the same sin is forgiven the first, second, and third time, but not the fourth. He brings two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says, when a person commits a sin, the first time he is forgiven, the second time he is forgiven, the third time he is forgiven, but the fourth time he is not forgiven. As it says: 'So says ה׳: for three sins of Israel, but for four I will not take it back.' And it says: 'All these things God does two or three times with a man.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that limits how many times ה׳ easily forgives the same sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that ה׳ easily forgives a repeated sin up to three times. The first פסוק (עמוס) shows that the fourth time is different. A second פסוק (איוב) is also quoted, and the next step asks why it was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
I will not take it back (I will not hold back the punishment)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean תשובה is impossible after the fourth time. It means ה׳ no longer forgives that sin as easily as He did the first three times.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם עוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה פַּעַם רִאשׁוֹנָה — מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ,
phrases.english: A person commits a sin the first time — he is forgiven,
the second time — he is forgiven,
the third time — he is forgiven,
the fourth time — he is not forgiven,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה פִּשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: as it says: 'So says the Lord: for three transgressions of Israel,
phrases.notes: עמוס ב:ו

phrases.english: but for four I will not take it back,'
(and it says:) 'Behold, all these things God does
phrases.notes: איוב לג:כט. The next step calls this 'and it says' (ואומר).

phrases.english: two or three times with a man.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about repeated sins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same sin is easily forgiven up to three times; the fourth time it is not.

steps.title: Why was a second verse needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא added 'and it says' with a second פסוק, since the first one seems enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for 'and it says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי בר יהודה brought a second proof. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק from עמוס already shows 'three yes, four no.' So the extra פסוק from איוב must be teaching something new. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it says' — the formula used to add a second proof-verse

phrases.english: What is the purpose of 'and it says'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the second proof-verse in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the second פסוק adds beyond the first.

steps.title: The second verse shows the rule applies to one person too
steps.stepSummary: The first פסוק speaks about all of ישראל, so one might think the rule is only for a ציבור. The second פסוק says 'with a man,' showing it applies to a יחיד too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say: this applies only to a community, but not to an individual. Come and hear: 'All these things God does two or three times with a man.' From then on he is not forgiven, as it says: 'For three transgressions of Israel, but for four I will not take it back.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the second פסוק teaches that the 'three times' rule also applies to one single person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in עמוס talks about 'ישראל', a whole nation, so it might only be about a community. The פסוק in איוב says 'with a man' (גבר), one person. Together they show the same rule for both, and the fourth time is still taken from עמוס.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible wrong idea)
These words apply (only to this case)

phrases.english: And if you would say: this applies only to a community,
phrases.notes: Because the first verse says 'Israel.'

phrases.english: but not to an individual,

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״הֶן כׇּל אֵלֶּה יִפְעַל אֵל
phrases.english: come and hear: 'Behold, all these things God does
two or three times with a man.'
phrases.notes: 'A man' = one individual.

phrases.english: (From here on he is not forgiven,
phrases.notes: This bracketed line repeats the source for the fourth time.

phrases.english: as it says: 'For three transgressions of Israel,
but for four I will not take it back.')

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second פסוק shows the three-times rule applies to an individual, not only to a community.
steps.whatToRemember: A repeated sin is easily forgiven three times, for a community and for an individual alike; the fourth time it is not.

steps.title: Do not confess again sins already confessed last יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that sins someone already confessed on one יום הכיפורים should not be confessed again on a later יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: sins that a person confessed on this יום הכיפורים, he should not confess on another יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about וידוי on יום הכיפורים. It gives the basic rule first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a person confessed a sin and was forgiven, the matter is closed. So he does not need to confess that sin again next year.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: sins that he confessed
phrases.notes: Sefaria notes this source is in the תוספתא.

phrases.english: on this Yom Kippur,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִתְוַדֶּה עֲלֵיהֶן יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אַחֵר.
phrases.english: he should not confess them on another Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about confessing on יום הכיפורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sins confessed on one יום הכיפורים are not confessed again on a later one.

steps.title: If he did the sin again, he must confess again
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds an exception: if the person did those same sins again, he must confess them on the next יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he did those sins again, he must confess on another יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives an exception to the rule from the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'do not confess again' only applies to sins that are finished. If he repeated the sin, it is a new sin, and he needs a new וידוי for it.

keyTerms.meaning: He repeated them (did those sins again)

phrases.english: But if he repeated them —
he must confess on another Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the rule in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sin that was repeated must be confessed again on the next יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: Confessing again for no reason is like a dog returning to its vomit
steps.stepSummary: If he did not repeat the sins but confessed them again anyway, the פסוק compares him to a dog returning to its vomit and a fool repeating his foolishness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he did not repeat them, but confessed them again, about him the verse says: 'Like a dog that returns to its vomit, so is a fool who repeats his foolishness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by criticizing someone who confesses again sins that were already forgiven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin was already forgiven, so bringing it up again is like going back to something disgusting that was already thrown out. The פסוק from משלי is used to show how improper this is.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and confessed again
Like a dog that returns to its vomit

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לֹא שָׁנָה בָּהֶן, וְחָזַר וְהִתְוַדָּה —
phrases.english: And if he did not repeat them, but went back and confessed —
about him the verse says:
phrases.notes: The word עֲלֵיהֶן appears in the printed text here; the sense is 'about him.'

phrases.english: 'As a dog that returns to its vomit,
phrases.notes: משלי כו:יא

phrases.english: so is a fool who repeats his foolishness.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם לֹא שָׁנָה בָּהֶן, וְחָזַר וְהִתְוַדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by describing the case where he confesses again without repeating the sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Confessing again sins already forgiven, without having repeated them, is criticized as foolish.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this ברייתא: confess a sin once. Confess it again only if you did it again. Bringing up a forgiven sin for no reason is like 'a dog returning to its vomit.'

steps.title: Confessing old sins again is praiseworthy
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees with the previous view. Re-confessing old sins is even more praiseworthy, as דוד said 'my sin is always before me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: All the more so, he is praiseworthy, as it says: 'For I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion in the ברייתא argues with what we just learned. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says that confessing the same old sins again on a later יום הכיפורים is a good thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view compared re-confessing to a dog returning to its vomit. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the opposite: keeping your past sins in front of you keeps you humble. His proof is דוד's words in תהלים, 'my sin is before me always.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
All the more so, he is praiseworthy,
phrases.notes: Meaning: one who confesses the old sins again.

phrases.english: as it says: 'For I know my transgressions'
'and my sin is before me always.'
phrases.notes: תהלים נא:ה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the view in steps 20-22 that re-confessing old sins is wrong.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Re-confessing previously confessed sins is praiseworthy.

steps.title: What about the dog-and-vomit verse?
steps.stepSummary: If re-confessing is praiseworthy, what does the פסוק 'like a dog returning to its vomit' mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do I explain the פסוק: 'Like a dog that returns to its vomit…'?
steps.whatsHappening: A problem is raised with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view used this פסוק to criticize re-confessing. If רבי אליעזר בן יעקב rejects that reading, he still has to explain what the פסוק is about.

keyTerms.meaning: how do I explain (literally: how do I fulfill) this verse
like a dog returning to its vomit

phrases.english: But how do I explain
'Like a dog that returns to its vomit, etc.'?
phrases.notes: משלי כו:יא

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 23 using the verse from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view that re-confessing is praiseworthy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse seems to condemn repeating something, so it needs another meaning if re-confessing is good.

steps.title: The verse refers to repeating the sin itself
steps.stepSummary: The verse follows רב הונא: when a person does a sin twice, it becomes permitted to him. The 'dog' is the one who repeats the sin, not the one who repeats the confession.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רב הונא. For רב הונא said: Once a person commits a sin and repeats it, it is permitted to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer moves the 'dog' verse onto a different person: someone who commits the same sin again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'dog returning to its vomit' is the sinner who goes back to his old sin. רב הונא describes how dangerous that is: after the second time, the sin starts to feel allowed. So the verse says nothing bad about re-confessing.

phrases.english: It follows Rav Huna.
For Rav Huna said:
Once a person commits a sin
and repeats it, it is permitted to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dog verse criticizes re-confessing old sins.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dog verse criticizes repeating the sin itself.

steps.title: Can a sin really become permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised. How can a sin become permitted just because someone did it twice?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It is permitted to him.' Could you really think so?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב הונא's statement. It sets up a correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing a sin twice cannot make it actually allowed by the תורה. So the words 'it is permitted' cannot be meant literally.

phrases.english: 'It is permitted to him' — could it enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רב הונא in step 25.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sin cannot become halachically permitted through repetition.

steps.title: It feels permitted to him
steps.stepSummary: The wording is corrected: the sin becomes to him like something permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: it becomes to him like something permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. The sin is not truly allowed; it only feels allowed to the sinner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא is describing what happens inside the sinner, not stating a law. After a sin is repeated, the person stops feeling it is wrong. That is why repeating a sin is like a dog going back to its vomit.
steps.whatToRemember: Re-confessing old sins: the first view says it is foolish, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says it is praiseworthy. For him, the 'dog' verse is about repeating the sin, which then feels permitted.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
it becomes to him like something permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem in step 26 by rewording רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sin only feels permitted to the sinner.

steps.title: One must spell out the sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בבא says a person must name his specific sin when confessing, like משה, who named the golden god.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one must spell out the sin, as it says: 'Please, this people has sinned a great sin, and they made themselves a god of gold.' These are the words of רבי יהודה בן בבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: how detailed must a confession be? רבי יהודה בן בבא says you must name the exact sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof is משה's prayer after the עגל. משה did not just say 'they sinned'; he named the sin: 'they made a god of gold.'

keyTerms.meaning: to spell out the specific sin
a god of gold (the golden calf)

phrases.english: And one must spell out the sin,
as it says: 'Please, this people has sinned'
'a great sin'
'and they made themselves a god of gold,'
phrases.notes: שמות לב:לא

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in the laws of וידוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person confessing must name the specific sin.

steps.title: Sins should stay covered
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees. 'Fortunate is he whose sin is covered' teaches that one should not spell out the sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'Fortunate is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the opposing view: you should not detail your sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק praises a person whose sin is 'covered.' So there is no need to say the details out loud, and keeping them hidden is better.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
'Fortunate is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.'
phrases.notes: תהלים לב:א

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה בן בבא in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One need not, and should not, spell out his sins.

steps.title: But משה did name the sin
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי עקיבא, why did משה say 'they made themselves a god of gold'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what is it that משה said: 'and they made themselves a god of gold'?
steps.whatsHappening: A challenge to רבי עקיבא from רבי יהודה בן בבא's proof verse. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה clearly named the sin. If sins should stay covered, רבי עקיבא's side has to explain why משה described it.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it that he said?

phrases.english: But what is it that Moshe said:
'and they made themselves a god of gold'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא (step 29) using the verse from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's view that sins are not spelled out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה explicitly named the sin of the golden god.

steps.title: משה was giving an excuse, not a confession
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי ינאי, משה mentioned the gold to defend the people: ה׳ gave them so much gold that it led them to make a golden god.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי ינאי. For רבי ינאי said: משה said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the world! The silver and gold You gave ישראל in such abundance, until they said 'Enough,' caused them to make a god of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer reads משה's words differently. He was not listing the sin; he was explaining why it happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'gold' is the point. משה argues that the huge wealth ה׳ gave them led them into the sin. So this verse is a defense, not a detailed confession, and it does not prove you must spell out sins.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה בן בבא: spell out the sin. רבי עקיבא: keep it covered. רבי עקיבא reads משה's words as an excuse, not a confession.

phrases.english: It follows Rabbi Yannai.
For Rabbi Yannai said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Moshe said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world!
The silver and gold that You gave Israel in abundance
until they said 'Enough'
caused them to make a god of gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 30.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה was spelling out Israel's sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה was defending Israel by blaming the abundance of gold.

steps.title: משה wanted his sin written; דוד did not
steps.stepSummary: Two great leaders took opposite approaches. משה asked that his sin be written in the תורה. דוד asked that his sin not be written, quoting 'fortunate is he whose sin is covered.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Two good leaders arose for Israel: משה and דוד. משה said: Let my failing be written, as it says: 'Because you did not believe in Me, to sanctify Me.' דוד said: Let my failing not be written, as it says: 'Fortunate is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an אגדה that matches the same debate about revealing or covering sins, using משה and דוד as examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's sin (at מי מריבה) is stated clearly in the תורה, so he wanted it known. דוד's own פסוק praises covering a sin. This shows both approaches can come from great people.

phrases.english: Two good leaders
arose for Israel: Moshe and David.
Moshe said: Let my failing be written,
as it says: 'Because you did not believe in Me, to sanctify Me,'
phrases.notes: במדבר כ:יב

phrases.english: David said: Let my failing not be written.
as it says: 'Fortunate is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי פַּרְנָסִים טוֹבִים עָמְדוּ לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an אגדה parallel to the debate in steps 28-29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה wanted his sin publicized; דוד wanted his sin covered.

steps.title: Parable of the two women being lashed
steps.stepSummary: Two women were lashed in court, one for a serious immoral sin and one for eating unripe שביעית figs. The second asked that her sin be announced so people would not think she did the worse sin. The court hung figs on her neck and announced her offense.
steps.simpleTranslation: A parable for משה and דוד: what is it like? Two women were lashed in court. One had sinned with immorality, and one had eaten unripe שביעית figs. The one who ate the figs said: Please, announce what I am being lashed for, so people won't say I am being lashed for the same thing as she is. They brought unripe שביעית figs, hung them on her neck, and announced before her: She is being lashed over שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains משה's choice with a parable. Like the woman with the figs, משה wanted his sin known so people would not think he sinned like his generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If משה's sin were left unstated, people might think he too was punished for the עגל or the מרגלים. Writing down his real, smaller sin protected his name. The parable explains משה's side; the גמרא does not explain דוד's reasoning here.

keyTerms.meaning: unripe fruit of the Sabbatical year

steps.whatToRemember: משה publicized his sin so no one would think he did the worse sins of his generation. Revealing a small sin can protect against a worse assumption.

phrases.english: A parable for Moshe and David:
What is the matter like?
To two women who were lashed in court.
One had sinned with immorality,
and one ate unripe figs of the Sabbatical year.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לָהֶן אוֹתָהּ שֶׁאָכְלָה פַּגֵּי שְׁבִיעִית:
phrases.english: The one who ate the unripe Sabbatical figs said to them:
Please, I ask of you,
announce what she (I) is being lashed for,
phrases.notes: She speaks of herself in the third person.

phrases.english: so that people will not say:

phrases.aramaic: עַל מַה שֶּׁזּוֹ לוֹקָה — זוֹ לוֹקָה.
phrases.english: For what that one is lashed, this one is lashed.
They brought unripe Sabbatical figs
and hung them on her neck,
and they announced before her, saying:
She is being lashed over matters of the Sabbatical year.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל דְּמֹשֶׁה וְדָוִד לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains with a parable why משה wanted his sin written (step 32).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Publicizing a lesser sin can prevent people from suspecting a worse one.

steps.title: Hypocrites must be exposed to prevent desecration of ה׳'s name
steps.stepSummary: We publicly expose חנפין (people who look righteous but are secretly wicked) because of חילול השם, based on a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We publicly expose hypocrites because of the desecration of ה׳'s name. As the פסוק says: 'When a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does wrong, I will put a stumbling block before him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new rule: a fake צדיק who secretly sins should be exposed publicly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step taught that sometimes a sin should be announced. Here is a case where it must be announced: if people think a sinner is a צדיק, they will copy him, and when the truth comes out, ה׳'s name is shamed. The פסוק teaches that ה׳ Himself puts a 'stumbling block' before such a person, meaning He brings his true nature into the open.

keyTerms.meaning: Hypocrites, people who act righteous but are secretly wicked

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean exposing every sinner. It is about a hypocrite whom the public mistakes for a צדיק. That mistake is exactly what causes the חילול השם.

phrases.english: One exposes the hypocrites
because of the desecration of God's name,
as it is stated: "When a righteous man turns from his righteousness
and commits iniquity, I will lay a stumbling block before him" (Ezekiel 3:20).
phrases.notes: ה׳ makes the hidden wickedness come out so people will not be misled.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְפַרְסְמִין אֶת הַחֲנֵפִין מִפְּנֵי חִילּוּל הַשֵּׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of when sins should be made public. After a case where the sinner herself asked for her sin to be announced, this gives a case where exposure is required.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hypocrites are exposed publicly to prevent חילול השם, based on 'I will lay a stumbling block before him.'

steps.title: Repentance of the completely wicked holds back punishment even after a sealed decree
steps.stepSummary: The תשובה of the totally wicked delays or prevents punishment, even when a גזר דין has already been sealed against them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The repentance of the completely wicked holds back punishment, even if a sentence of punishment has already been sealed against them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא teaches a new point about the power of תשובה, even for the worst sinners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that once a person is 'completely wicked' and his punishment is already sealed, it is too late. This teaching says no: real תשובה can still stop the punishment. This fits the main theme of the whole סוגיא, the greatness of תשובה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This strongly encourages תשובה. No one should give up and think his fate is already fixed.

phrases.english: The repentance of the utterly wicked
holds back the punishment,
and even though there was sealed against him
a sentence of judgment for punishment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching in the same list. It moves from exposing sinners to the power of their תשובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תשובה of the totally wicked can prevent punishment even after a sealed decree.

steps.title: The calm comfort of the wicked ends in their downfall
steps.stepSummary: When רשעים live in peace and comfort, it leads to their ruin in the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: The calm comfort of the wicked ends in disaster.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short warning: an easy, comfortable life for wicked people is a trap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comfort can look like a blessing. But for רשעים, free time and ease give them room to think about and do more sin, and that leads to their destruction (תקלה).

phrases.english: The tranquility of the wicked ends in their downfall,
phrases.notes: In their comfort they sit and think about forbidden things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another short teaching in the same list about sin and its results.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The peace and comfort of רשעים ultimately leads to their ruin.

steps.title: Authority buries the one who holds it
steps.stepSummary: Power and leadership are dangerous to whoever holds them. A person enters power with nothing and leaves with nothing. The best hope is to leave as free of sin as when he entered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Authority buries its owner. He enters it naked and leaves it naked. If only his leaving could be like his entering, free of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא warns about the spiritual danger of holding power (רשות).
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Buries its owner' means power can shorten a person's life or ruin him. 'Naked' means you gain nothing lasting from the position. The real wish is not to profit but simply to leave without having added sins.

phrases.english: And authority buries the one who holds it,
naked he enters into it
and naked he will leave it,
and if only his leaving would be like his entering.
phrases.notes: That is, leaving his position without sin, just as he came in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the warnings. After the danger of comfort for רשעים, it turns to the danger of power.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Authority endangers its holder, and the best he can hope for is to leave it without added sin.

steps.title: What רב said to himself on the way to judge
steps.stepSummary: On his way to court, רב reminded himself that judging puts his life at risk, earns nothing for his family, and that he should hope to come home as free of sin as he left.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב went out to judge cases, he would say: 'By his own choice he goes out toward death. He does not provide for his household's needs. He goes home empty-handed. If only his coming home would be like his going out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story showing how רב lived the lesson that 'authority buries its owner.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A דיין who judges wrongly is punished by Heaven, so רב said he was walking 'toward death' by choice. Judges took no pay, so he brought nothing home. רב's wish matches the previous teaching: just to return without sin.
steps.confusionAlert: רב's words reverse the earlier phrase ('entering like leaving' instead of 'leaving like entering'). Here he is talking about leaving his home and returning to it. He hopes to come back home as sinless as he left.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how great judges treated their role: with fear and humility, not as a source of honor or profit.

phrases.english: When Rav would go out
to judge a case, he would say this:
By his own will he goes out to death,
phrases.notes: A judge who rules wrongly is liable to death at the hands of Heaven.

phrases.english: and the needs of his household he does not provide,
and empty-handed he goes to his household,
phrases.notes: A judge takes no salary.

phrases.english: and if only his coming home would be like his going out.
phrases.notes: That is, coming home without sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כִּי הֲוָה נָפֵיק לְמֵידַן דִּינָא אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the previous teaching about the danger of authority lived out by רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב approached judging with fear: it risks his life, brings no profit, and his only wish was to return without sin.

steps.title: Introducing what רבא said on the way to judge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to quote what רבא used to say when he went out to judge. His words continue in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבא would go out to judge, he would say this:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to tell us רבא's words, a parallel to רב's saying, which come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting רבא's practice right after רב's shows that more than one great אמורא felt this fear about judging. The actual content of רבא's words comes in the following text.

phrases.english: When Rava would go out
to judge, he would say this:

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא כִּי הֲוָה נָפֵיק לְדִינָא אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a parallel story to רב's, introducing רבא's saying before going to court.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רבא's personal statement before judging. The content continues on the next עמוד.
